office_does: One of the 2nd District's two members of the Washington House, voting on state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets for a two-year term.
race_blurb: Ten-year Republican incumbent and Transportation ranking member Andrew Barkis faces first-time candidate William Dehnel, a Pierce Transit supervisor and union officer who prefers the Labor Democrat Party. They split most sharply on the 2026 millionaires' tax and on LGBTQ+ and school policy.

candidates.summary: State representative since 2016 and Lacey property-management owner, running on transportation maintenance, housing supply, and opposition to income and gas tax increases.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346 (2026 tax on income over $1 million) and the 2025 B&O and services tax bills [S5][S8][S9]
Calls himself a vocal opponent of state income taxes and gas tax increases [S3]
Advocates more housing supply and fewer barriers to development; endorsed by realtor and rental-housing groups [S3][S4]

taxes.basis: Voted against ESSB 6346, ESHB 2081 and ESSB 5814 and says he opposes state income taxes and gas tax increases.

spending.basis: Emphasizes fiscally responsible budgets and fighting deficit spending that outpaces revenue.

housing.basis: Advocates increased supply and removing bureaucratic barriers, opposed frequent building-code updates; backed by real-estate and rental-housing groups.

safety.basis: Says he worked to stop shortening sentences for serious crimes and to keep accountability for registered offenders; law-enforcement endorsements.

experience.basis: In the House since 2016 and Transportation ranking member, against a first-time candidate.

social.basis: Voted against ESSB 5599 and is endorsed by Human Life PAC; no campaign statement on the topic.

parental-rights.basis: Voted against ESHB 1296's changes to the I-2081 parental-rights list and added a parental right to request charter-school enrollment; no campaign statement.

candidates.summary: Pierce Transit dispatch supervisor and ATU Local 758 officer in his first run for office, campaigning on progressive taxation, school and rural healthcare funding, and LGBTQ+ protections.
highlights: Says he fully supports the 9.9% tax on income over $1 million and wants a system that asks more of those who have more [S4]
Opposes I-1 and I-638 by name [S7]
Would fully fund special education and restore early-learning funding cut in 2026 [S5]
Endorsed by the Washington State Labor Council and Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates [S8][S9]

taxes.basis: Explicitly supports the millionaires' income tax and repeatedly calls for taxes that ask more of those who have more.

spending.basis: Calls for closing the special-education funding gap, restoring early learning, and more investment in rural clinics and infrastructure.

healthcare.basis: Proposals work within the existing system (protect Apple Health, fund clinics, drug-price negotiation); no single-payer plank.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with union but no public office, running against a ten-year incumbent.

social.basis: Opposes I-638, would protect gender-affirming care and anti-discrimination law, and pledges never to vote for legislation targeting LGBTQ+ people.

parental-rights.basis: Opposes I-1, citing student privacy and the risk of outing LGBTQ+ students to parents.
